latest_release.name: v3.2.1
latest_release.body:
# Release Notes

This release adds `@defer` support to Caliban Gateway and fixes queries with repeated fragment spreads taking exponential time to process. It also includes a few bug fixes and forks fewer fibers per gateway request.

## New Features
* Added `@defer` support to the gateway, enabled by default and using the `deferSpec=20220824` format, by @ghostdogpr in https://github.com/ghostdogpr/caliban/pull/3160

## Bug Fixes
* Fixed exponential processing of queries that spread the same fragments several times at each level, in `maxDepth`, `maxFields`, cost estimation, cache control and the gateway, by @ghostdogpr in https://github.com/ghostdogpr/caliban/pull/3160
* Fixed recursive `@oneOf` input types, whose schema never finished building, by @ghostdogpr in https://github.com/ghostdogpr/caliban/pull/3140
* Fixed `@interfaceObject` support in the gateway, for `Gateway.fromSupergraph` and for `Subgraph.federation` without SDL, by @ghostdogpr in https://github.com/ghostdogpr/caliban/pull/3137
* Fixed `@defer` multipart responses in the Quick and Tapir adapters, where the delimiter ending a part was only sent once the next part was ready, by @xsistens in https://github.com/ghostdogpr/caliban/pull/3148
* Stopped using `$` in variable names generated by the client codegen, which failed to compile on Scala 3.9 with `-Werror`, by @ghostdogpr in https://github.com/ghostdogpr/caliban/pull/3181

**Note:** the gateway now rejects operations that select more than 100,000 fields once their fragments are expanded. Use `GatewayConfig.withMaxOperationFields` to change this limit. `GatewayConfig` has a new field, so its `copy` and `apply` signatures change.

## Performance Improvements
* Reduced the fibers forked per gateway request from 51 to 24 on the ChilliCream gateway benchmark, using 7% less CPU per request, by @ghostdogpr in https://github.com/ghostdogpr/caliban/pull/3145

## Other Small Improvements
* Set `PaginationError` as the `innerThrowable` of the errors returned for rejected pagination arguments, so that wrappers can identify them, by @ghostdogpr in https://github.com/ghostdogpr/caliban/pull/3180
* Stitched queries that reuse a fragment's fields in several places now contain generated fragments (`F0`, `F1`, …) by @ghostdogpr in https://github.com/ghostdogpr/caliban/pull/3160
* The tracer's `document` attribute is now the operation itself, with its real operation type, instead of wrapping the root as `query{{…}}`, by @ghostdogpr in https://github.com/ghostdogpr/caliban/pull/3160

# Caliban

[![Release Artifacts][Badge-SonatypeReleases]][Link-SonatypeReleases]
[![Badge-Discord]][Link-Discord]

[Link-SonatypeReleases]: https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/com.github.ghostdogpr/caliban_3 "Sonatype Releases"
[Badge-SonatypeReleases]: https://img.shields.io/maven-central/v/com.github.ghostdogpr/caliban_3 "Sonatype Releases"
[Link-Discord]: https://discord.gg/2ccFBr4 "Discord"
[Badge-Discord]: https://img.shields.io/discord/629491597070827530?logo=discord "chat on discord"

Caliban is a purely functional library for building GraphQL servers and clients in Scala.
 
The design principles behind the library are the following:
- minimal amount of boilerplate: no need to manually define a schema for every type in your API.
- high performance: while every public interface is pure and immutable, library internals have been optimized for speed.
- clean separation between schema definition and implementation: schema is defined and validated at compile time using Scala standard types, resolver (`RootResolver`) is a simple value provided at runtime.

### Consult the [Documentation](https://ghostdogpr.github.io/caliban/) to learn how to use Caliban.

### Any questions? Head up to the [#caliban](https://discordapp.com/channels/629491597070827530/633200096393166868) channel on [ZIO Discord](https://discord.gg/EYpumuv).
